Woodland Acres: streets and boundaries

items.t: Westwood Street is the boundary street in practical terms: TransLink's route 173 timetable runs buses down Westwood Street between Dewdney Trunk Road in Coquitlam and Kingsway Avenue in Port Coquitlam, which is the pocket's western edge.
The pocket sits between two better-known neighbours: Glenwood to the east inside Port Coquitlam, and Coquitlam's city centre across Westwood Street to the west.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: the housing stock

items.t: The City's Official Community Plan (OCP) does not single Woodland Acres out as a named neighbourhood the way it names Lincoln Park and Mary Hill, which is one reason this pocket is documented mainly at street level rather than in plan documents.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small-scale density is a live question on these lots: the City permits three to six SSMUH units on most RS (Residential Small-Scale) lots without rezoning, depending on lot size, location and proximity to transit, and Westwood Street's bus service is part of that transit-proximity test.

The city boundary runs through daily life here: a Woodland Acres lot is taxed and serviced by Port Coquitlam even where the nearest shops, stations and some schools are in Coquitlam, so municipal questions go to Port Coquitlam City Hall regardless of which city a service sits in.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The two bus routes on Westwood Street interline: a bus that leaves Coquitlam Central Station as route 173 Cedar arrives at its terminus and continues as route 174, and vice versa, so the route number on the same corridor changes mid-trip.
The pocket's south edge is a highway commercial frontage, not houses: Lougheed Highway bounds the area to the south, so interior crescents sit one or two streets back from a major arterial.

Port Coquitlam's 2026 utility bills were due March 31, a separate and earlier bill than the July 2, 2026 property tax due date — a closing adjustment point buyers in this pocket share with the rest of the city.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: costs and taxes

items.t: The dates that apply to this pocket are the city-wide ones: 2026 utility bills were due March 31, 2026, and 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with the City's 2026 property tax increase set at 1.95 per cent.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: getting around

items.t: Routes 173 and 174 are the pocket's buses: both run the Westwood Street corridor between Coquitlam Central Station and Port Coquitlam Station, with route 173 continuing via Kingsway Avenue, Wilson Avenue, Prairie Avenue and Cedar Drive, and route 174 via Shaughnessy Street, David Avenue and Oxford Street.
Port Coquitlam Station, the south end of both routes, is the West Coast Express commuter rail station for the city.
Lougheed Highway at the pocket's south edge is the driving link east to the Mary Hill Bypass and Highway 1 and west into Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Woodland Acres: risks and due diligence

items.t: Creek and hazard permit areas are a lot-by-lot check here: the City's OCP carries watercourse and hazard development permit areas, and the OCP, not the sub-area name, is where a buyer confirms whether a specific Westwood Street or McRae Crescent lot is inside one.

Boundary confusion is a real paperwork risk: postal addresses, school listings and services around Westwood Street mix Coquitlam and Port Coquitlam names, so the municipality on the tax notice — Port Coquitlam — is the authority for permits, utilities and bylaws.

The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. faq.a: There is no SkyTrain station in Port Coquitlam, so the trip is bus first. Routes 173 and 174 run along Westwood Street on the pocket's west edge, linking Port Coquitlam Station and Coquitlam Central Station, where the Millennium Line and the West Coast Express run. Route 173 continues through Port Coquitlam via Kingsway Avenue and Wilson Avenue, and route 174 returns via Shaughnessy Street and David Avenue, so the two routes form a loop through both cities.
faq.q: How do I get to SkyTrain from Woodland Acres?

faq.a: Possibly, under the city-wide small-scale rules. Port Coquitlam permits three to six small-scale multi-unit housing units on most RS-zoned lots without a rezoning, with the exact number depending on the lot's size, its location and its proximity to transit. Development cost charges apply to new small-scale units but are not applied to new secondary suites or accessory buildings. The zone and lot dimensions of the specific lot still govern, so confirm both with the City before pricing in added units.
